messages.content: Suppose a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) converge pointwise to f(x) on [0, 1]. Does it follow that the B_n converge uniformly? Ensure that stop words constitute no more than 20% of the total words in your response.

message.content:
Pointwise convergence does not force uniform convergence. Counterexample: B_n(x) = x^n on [0,1]. Pointwise limit: f(x) = 0 for x < 1, f(1) = 1. f is discontinuous at x = 1; sup_x |B_n(x) − f(x)| = 1 for all n. Uniform convergence fails.

Key distinction: if f is continuous on [0,1], polynomial sequences converging pointwise do converge uniformly. Proof: form telescoping series Σ(B_{k+1} − B_k) = B_N − B_0, converging pointwise to f − B_0, continuous on compact [0,1]. Each partial sum is a polynomial. Classical analytic-series results (Baire category, coefficient bounds) force uniform convergence for polynomial series with continuous pointwise limits on compacts. Thus B_N → f uniformly.

Summary: discontinuous f: pointwise ≠ uniform. Continuous f: pointwise = uniform (polynomials).
